output.summary: KEP-580 Pod Ready++ adds extensibility to pod readiness so that external feedback, not only container readiness from kubelet probes, can be injected into PodStatus and influence whether a pod is considered ready. The KEP is implemented and at stable stage.
output.rationale: Pod readiness is set only by kubelet readiness probes, yet Services, endpoints, and rolling updates depend on it, so a new pod can be reported ready before its load balancer or network path is programmed, risking disruption. The proposal lets external signals feed into pod readiness so higher-level controllers and services wait for them. The design excerpt rejects fixing every workload controller as too large a change, and rejects extending container readiness because it ties external feedback to low-level runtime constructs.

alternatives.option: Fix each workload controller to handle the readiness gap
alternatives.why_not: Source says: "Solving this problem in all workload controllers would require much bigger change than this proposal."

alternatives.option: Extend container readiness with external feedback
alternatives.why_not: Source says: "Injecting external feedback into container status would complicate the abstraction and control flow."

alternatives.option: Provide a generic framework for all transition problems such as blue green deployment
alternatives.why_not: Listed as a non-goal in the design document; the KEP is scoped to extra signals for pod readiness only.

evidence.quote: Besides container readiness, external feedback can be injected into PodStatus and influence pod readiness.
Pod readiness is dictated by kubelet with user specified readiness probe.
Solving this problem in all workload controllers would require much bigger change than this proposal.
Injecting external feedback into container status would complicate the abstraction and control flow.
